# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor (core)

**Recreated in the core repo.** This epic was moved from `tce-main-street`
(`MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19`, deleted on migration) because the story-line engine now
lives in core (`src/story-line/`, shipped by `CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B`). The
original producer decisions are carried forward unchanged: **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**, **Q2 = A (epic decomposed into vertical slices)**, **Q3 = A
(curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

The branching story-line mechanic is now a first-class core module
(`src/story-line/`: types, `compile`, `resolve`, `journal`, `ui-adapter`, plus
the `@story-line` alias and the Gym `GymStorylineScene` demo). What did **not**
move is authoring: the content CSV model, the transactional author API, the
static validator and the manifest/Mermaid graph generator are still
Main-Street-only code (`tce-main-street` `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`,
`validate-storylines.ts`, `storyline-graph.ts`, `render-storyline-graph.ts`)
wired to Main Street card columns (coins/reputation deltas, `storylineId`,
`storylineTitle`).

Consequently a content designer for **any** TCE game that uses story-lines can
still only hand-edit a game-local CSV or drive a game-local CLI, and can only
see the arc as a generated Mermaid/JSON/`SVG` artefact. They cannot *see* the arc
they are editing, cannot discover dangling targets visually, and cannot make a
guided, validated edit in one place.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers (any TCE game)** — see a storyline's shape at
  a glance, inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename,
  retarget a link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV
  internals.
- **TCE core engineers** — trust that every edit goes through one validated,
  transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync with the
  game's content CSV.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write a
  dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a game developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool driven by my
  game's content adapter, excluded from the game build and reusing the same
  author API, so it adds no runtime dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### 0. Content and authoring toolchain generalised into core (prerequisite)

The editor must not depend on Main-Street-only code, so the authoring seams the
original epic assumed are part of this epic's scope:

1. A generic **content model** over the core story-line types: parse/serialise
   the game content CSV, a **content adapter** seam for game-specific columns
   (Main Street's coins/reputation deltas, `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`,
   `hasChoices`/accept/reject), and a content checksum for change detection.
2. A generic **manifest builder** and Mermaid **graph generator** (deterministic,
   timestamp-free) producing the same node/edge/storyline/cycle shape the
   editor's view model consumes.
3. A generic **static validator** with a formattable report (cycles
   informational, opt-in failure on cycle).
4. A generic **transactional author API**: build the edited CSV in memory,
   validate, then write atomically; `--dry-run` supported; the **only** writer.
5. Thin `tsx` CLIs over each seam (core tooling runs on `tsx`, not `vite-node`).

Parity requirement: extracting these seams must not change Main Street's shipped
storylines or CSV formats; the existing Main-Street storyline suites stay green
while it migrates onto the core seams.

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

6. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite toolchain (no new runtime dependency). It is
   a development tool and must not be included in the game or Electron build.
   The tool takes the game's content CSV / adapter as a launch argument so it is
   game-agnostic.
7. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and node
   selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

8. A Node-side bridge over the core author/validator/graph seams: preview/diff
   before write, validate-before-write, artefact regeneration after an accepted
   edit, and a concurrency guard (content hash).

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

9. Edit an existing card's fields through the content adapter's generic field
   descriptors (core-editable: name, effect text, choice flag, accept/reject
   successor links, storyline id/title; game columns such as coin/reputation
   deltas come from the adapter).
10. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
    pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

11. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
    group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
12. Documentation covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow, validation and
    artefact regeneration (core engine reference + developer tooling docs), and
    the note in `tce-main-street` that its authoring tooling now consumes core.
13. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test for
    the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor -- --help` exits 0
   from the core repo root on the existing toolchain with no new runtime
   dependency; the command is documented in the core docs. Verified by a test
   that invokes the entry point and asserts it exits 0.
2. **Game-agnostic content source** — the editor loads a game's content CSV and
   field mapping through the content adapter; no Main Street import appears in
   the editor or the core authoring seams. Verified by a unit test over a
   synthetic fixture plus an import-boundary check.
3. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the generated
   manifest: all nodes and edges appear, choice cards are visually distinct,
   storyline grouping and cycle edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its
   links/metadata. Covered by a browser test.
4. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the generated manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and its JSON
   schema.
5. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through the core author
   API. A test asserts no editor module writes the content CSV except through
   that module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
6. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
7. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates the committed Mermaid/JSON manifest artefacts (and any generated
   per-game doc artefacts the game opts into), and the `--check` drift guards
   pass. Edits that touch hand-written documented rows surface an explicit
   "manual documentation update required" result naming the failing check.
   Covered by tests.
8. **Concurrency guard** — if the content CSV changed on disk since load, the
   editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
9. **Build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the production
   game bundle or the packaged Electron app; verified by a build/test assertion
   (the editor entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts`
   graph).
10. **All related documentation is updated** — core engine reference, developer
    tooling docs, code comments, and the Main Street note that its authoring
    tooling consumes the core seams.
11. **Full project test suite must pass** — `npm test`
   (`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`: unit + browser + tutorial E2E + Electron smoke)
    is green, and the Main Street storyline suites stay green.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — one transactional, self-validating author operation in
  core; no second way to edit content CSVs.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`tsx`/Vitest/Playwright
  toolchain; the generic module stays Phaser-free and game-import-free.
- **Consumable by games** — core ships the seams and a default content adapter;
  games supply their own adapter (column mapping) and content CSV.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — manifest/Mermaid generators must stay
  timestamp-free so existing drift guards keep passing.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Behaviour preservation** — extraction must not change Main Street's shipped
  storylines (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) or CSV formats; RNG seed
  replays stay identical.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — conditional/cost-gated option semantics
  (`MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) stay out of scope; the editor edits today's curated
  choice model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (core repo research, verified)

- **Generic runtime** — `src/story-line/` (`compile.ts`, `resolve.ts`,
  `journal.ts`, `ui-adapter.ts`, `types.ts`, `index.ts`), exported through the
  `@story-line` alias (`resolveCoreAliases`, `tsconfig.json`, scaffold template).
  Generic CSV `options` encoding and legacy `hasChoices` compilation already
  exist here; there is **no** manifest, validator, author or graph seam.
- **Tests** — `tests/story-line/{compile,resolve,journal,ui-adapter}.test.ts`
  with `tests/story-line/helpers.ts` (in-memory engine-adapter double, no game
  dependency).
- **Docs** — `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (module, adapters, Gym demo).
- **Demo** — `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` (registered, smoke
  covered).
- **Tooling conventions** — core CLIs are `tsx` scripts under `scripts/`
  (`npx tsx scripts/...`) and `npm test` runs `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  (unit → browser → tutorial E2E → Electron smoke); Vitest projects `unit`
  (`tests/**/*.test.ts`) and `browser` (`tests/**/*.browser.test.ts`) are
  configured in the root `vite.config.ts`. `ajv` and Playwright are existing
  devDependencies.
- **Gap** — no authoring toolchain in core; Main Street still owns the only
  author/validator/manifest/graph implementations.
- **Source of the seams to generalise** — `tce-main-street`
  `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`parseCsv`, `addCard`, `linkCard`,
  `applyToFile`, `parseAuthorArgs`), `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`
  (`validateStorylines`, `formatStorylineReport`, `storylineReportToJson`),
  `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` (`buildStorylineManifest`,
  `serializeManifest`, `renderMermaid`, `filterManifestByStoryline`,
  `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`, `describeEventImpact`,
  `describeChoiceRouting`), `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts`,
  `src/CsvChecksum.ts` (`computeCsvChecksum`), and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`.

## Desired change

1. **Generalise** the content/authoring seams into core behind a content
   adapter, with parity tests against the Main Street behaviour.
2. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   seams.
3. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.
4. **Guided editing** — edit card fields and add/relink cards through forms that
   preview the diff and validate before write.
5. **Stay in sync** — regenerate the committed artefacts after accepted edits
   and guard against concurrent external CSV edits.
6. **Document and test** — authoring walkthrough, unit tests for the
   bridge/view-model and a browser round-trip test.

**Recommended slice order for planning** (per Q2 = A): (S0) generalise the
content/authoring toolchain → (S1) host + read-only viewer → (S2) write bridge +
preview/validate → (S3) curated edit forms → (S4) storyline management +
docs/tests polish.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — **new** generic content model + adapter
  seam.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — **new** parse/serialise + content checksum.
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — **new** manifest builder + Mermaid
  generator.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — **new** validator + report formatting.
- `src/story-line/content/author.ts` — **new** transactional author API.
- `scripts/storyline-author.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI over the author API.
- `scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI over the manifest generator.
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI over the validator.
- `scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** editor entry point.
- `scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` — **new** host + API bridge.
- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — **new** manifest → view model.
- `tools/storyline-editor/` — **new** editor page + SVG graph renderer.
- `tests/story-line/editor/` — **new** unit + browser tests and fixtures.
- `./vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor host config (does not
  touch the game/build config).
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — **edit** authoring + editor sections.
- `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — **new** developer/content-designer
  walkthrough.
- `./package.json` — **edit** add the `storylines:*` scripts.

## Migration notes and assumptions

- **Why moved** — the runtime engine now ships from core
  (`CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B` / `CSS-…` extraction round), so an editor for it belongs
  with the engine, not with one game.
- **Assumption: the authoring toolchain must be generalised first.** Only the
  runtime module moved; the author/validator/manifest/graph code is still
  Main-Street-only. Child T0 was added for this (it did not exist in the original
  plan) and blocks the viewer work. If the producer would rather keep the
  authoring toolchain game-side, this epic collapses back to a Main Street tool.
- **Assumption: game-specific columns stay in the game adapter.** Core edits the
  generic story-line fields; coin/reputation deltas and other game columns are
  described by the game's adapter. Main Street's existing behaviour (and its
  `set-storyline` gap: the CLI documents it but implements only `add-card` and
  `link`, so storyline assignment goes through `linkCard`'s
  `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`) is preserved by parity tests.
- **Assumption: toolchain** — core CLIs use `tsx` (not `vite-node`), and the
  editor's content source is a path argument, so the Main Street `?raw` CSV
  import constraint does not apply.
- **Effort/risk inherited** from the original item (`Severe` risk, `Large`
  effort). The S0 prerequisite adds scope, so both should be re-run with
  `/skill:effort-and-risk` before implementation starts.
- **Original item** `MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19` and its six children
  (`MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT`, `MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47`, `MS-0MUSY1O8V008F9BO`,
  `MS-0MUSY1QAS007AREL`, `MS-0MUSY1S54000GPIT`, `MS-0MUSY1UIR007XLOQ`) were
  deleted from the `tce-main-street` worklog in the same change; all content was
  carried into this tree.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B** — "Generic story-line system in core (module, parity
  tests, Gym demo, docs)" — the extraction this epic follows.
- **CG-0MVHY82PQ004Q3B9** — "Manually test the story-line extraction (Gym demo +
  Main Street storylines)".
- `tce-main-street` `MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI` — "Extract the storyline features"
  (provenance of the core module).
- `tce-main-street` `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` (parent that shipped the validator,
  graph/manifest export and authoring helper), `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` (authoring
  helper CLI), `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` (graph/manifest export & JSON schema),
  `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` (static validator & npm gate), `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U`
  (behaviour regression harness), `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C` (Mermaid→SVG docs
  render), `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9` (conditional/cost-gated options — out of scope).
- **Gym** `GymStorylineScene` — the demo whose content is the natural first
  fixture for the generic editor.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Carried forward (producer, original intake — unchanged)

- **Q1 — Delivery form / host.** Options: (A) in-repo local web tool; (B) in-game
  developer overlay; (C) standalone Electron tool. **Final accepted answer: A —
  in-repo local web tool.**
- **Q2 — Work-item shape & first increment.** Options: (A) epic decomposed into
  vertical slices; (B) single feature; (C) read-only MVP only. **Final accepted
  answer: A — epic**, decomposed into vertical slices (viewer → write bridge →
  edit forms → storyline management + docs/tests).
- **Q3 — Editing interaction model.** Options: (A) curated form/guided editor;
  (B) direct-manipulation graph editor; (C) both. **Final accepted answer: A —
  curated form/guided editor**, with diff/preview and validate-before-write; no
  free-form canvas manipulation.
- **Q0 — Write path.** Reuse the single transactional author API; never add a
  second CSV edit path.
- **Q0b — Artefacts.** Regenerate the committed manifest/Mermaid artefacts after
  an accepted edit; the `--check` drift guard and doc-drift checks must pass.

### Open (non-blocking)

- **Q4 — Should the authoring toolchain live in core at all, or stay game-side
  with only the editor shell being generic?** Recommended: generalise it into
  core behind a content adapter (child T0), so story-line authoring is reusable
  the same way the runtime now is. Recorded as the plan's working assumption;
  changeable before implementation.

# Create a dedicated TCE Discord channel and repoint the release-notification webhook

## Headline

Create a Discord channel dedicated to Tableau Card Engine and repoint the TCE release-notification webhook at that channel, so every `dev`→`main` release announcement lands in a TCE-owned channel that the community can follow. Item is assigned to the **Producer**, who performs the Discord-side steps.

## Problem statement

TCE release announcements are posted by the ship skill (`discord-notify.js`) through a project-private webhook, but TCE has no clearly dedicated channel of its own for those announcements, so the project has no single, discoverable "follow TCE releases here" location. Creating a dedicated channel and repointing the existing webhook gives releases a stable home and removes the ambiguity about where a TCE announcement belongs.

## Users

- **Community / players** — follow TCE release news in one dedicated place.
  - As a community member I want a TCE-specific channel so I can follow releases without filtering other projects' traffic.
- **Producer / maintainers** — publish releases without thinking about routing.
  - As the producer I want the release webhook bound to the TCE channel so an announcement can never land in a shared or generic channel.
- **Future game repos** — reuse the pattern (per-project channel + project-private webhook).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Dedicated channel exists.** A Discord channel dedicated to TCE exists in the chosen server, its **guild id, channel id and name are recorded on this work item**, and its purpose/topic states that it carries TCE release announcements.
2. **Webhook points at the new channel.** The TCE release webhook (a webhook named `Tableau Card Engine` created in the new channel, or the existing one repointed to it) is installed, and `discord.webhook_url` in the TCE per-project private config resolves to it. Verified objectively: `GET https://discord.com/api/webhooks/<id>` returns the **new** `channel_id` (and expected `guild_id`). Token value is never recorded — redacted as `[REDACTED]`.
3. **Delivery proven.** A test notification (a minimal release-shaped payload, or a `sendReleaseNotification` call) is delivered and visibly appears in the **new** channel only; the old target receives nothing new. Result recorded on the item.
4. **Old target dispositioned.** The previous webhook is either deleted in the Discord UI (recommended) or explicitly retained as a documented fallback — the decision and rationale are recorded, and no dangling config references a channel that is no longer used.
5. **Secrets stay out of git.** No webhook URL or token is committed, logged or pasted into a work-item comment; `.worklog/` remains gitignored (`.gitignore` line 105) and the private config keeps mode `0600`; the tracked `.worklog/config.yaml` carries no webhook.
6. **Precedence intact.** Config precedence in `discord-notify.js` (project private → project tracked → global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`) still resolves the new webhook for TCE; the global fallback is left unchanged (or, if changed, the change is recorded here).
7. **Validation is repeatable.** A copy-pasteable verification command (resolve the configured webhook, assert `channel_id`) is recorded on the item and documented, so the next maintainer can re-check routing without guesswork; the next real release posting to the new channel is confirmed after it happens.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically a short "Release notifications (Discord)" note in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (channel, config precedence, verification command, secret handling) plus the config-file comment naming the channel.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer performs the Discord-side work.** No Discord bot/user token exists on this machine (searched: environment variables, `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`, every project `.worklog` store), so channel + webhook creation is done by hand in the Discord client. If credentials are supplied later, the same ACs are satisfiable via `POST /guilds/{id}/channels` and `POST /channels/{id}/webhooks`.
- **Never commit the webhook.** TCE's whole `.worklog/` tree is gitignored; keep the URL only in `.worklog/config.private.yaml` (mode `0600`).
- **Scope is the TCE core repo only.** Do not touch `../tce-main-street/.worklog/config.private.yaml` (a separate webhook in a separate guild) or the global fallback unless the operator explicitly extends scope.
- **Leave notification semantics alone.** The ship skill's non-blocking contract (a failed post never fails a release) must not change; this is a routing change, not a code change.
- **No behaviour change to the release pipeline.** `discord-notify.js` is a read-only reference for precedence and payload shape; modify it only if the Producer decides a code change is warranted (which would need its own ACs).

## Existing state

- `.worklog/config.private.yaml` (gitignored, mode `0600`) is the only live TCE Discord config and holds the single key `discord.webhook_url`.
- Current webhook: `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1552679891349274647/[REDACTED]`. Live probe (`GET` on the webhook) returns `name: "Tableau Card Engine"`, `guild_id: 1149235410300588062`, `channel_id: 1149896861096882256`; the webhook was created 2026-09-24, the guild 2023-09-07, that channel 2023-09-09.
- Two guilds are in play, which is why the target server is a Producer decision (see Appendix):
  - **1149235410300588062** — where the TCE release webhook posts today.
  - **728852904978415676 ("Wizards Code")** — where the public invite `https://discord.gg/gUKQTFkzQ4` resolves (channel `general_devlogs`, `849855725538902046`), and where the Main Street project's webhook posts.
- Tracked `.worklog/config.yaml` holds `projectName: Tableau-Card-Engine`, `prefix: CG`, `autoSync: false`, `cta: "[Play the alpha release](…). Provide feedback in [Discord](https://discord.gg/gUKQTFkzQ4)"` — no webhook, and no other Discord reference exists in TCE source or docs (only `CHANGELOG.md` renders the `cta` line).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Deployment / Release" points at `RELEASE.md` but documents nothing about release notifications; the ship skill's `SKILL.md` § "Discord release notification" is the only written reference.

## Desired change

Producer-executed runbook (order matters; result of each step recorded on the item):

1. **Choose the server** (see Appendix OPEN QUESTION) and create a text channel dedicated to TCE — recommended name `#tableau-card-engine`, under the existing TCE/games category if one exists; set the channel topic to "Tableau Card Engine release announcements".
2. **Create an incoming webhook** in that channel (`Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks`), named `Tableau Card Engine`; copy the URL (do not paste the token anywhere except the private config).
3. **Repoint the config**: replace `discord.webhook_url` in `.worklog/config.private.yaml`, keep mode `0600`, and add a comment naming the channel/guild so the target is obvious without decoding the URL.
4. **Verify routing** with the recorded command:
   ```bash
   cd /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine
   WH=$(grep 'webhook_url' .worklog/config.private.yaml | sed 's/.*webhook_url: *//')
   curl -s "$WH" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k: d.get(k) for k in ("name", "channel_id", "guild_id")})'
   ```
   Expect the new `channel_id`. Assert it against the value recorded in step 1.
5. **Post a test notification** to prove delivery (payload shaped like the release embed: version, tag, release date, PR link, short changelog excerpt) and confirm it lands in the new channel; confirm the old channel shows nothing new.
6. **Dispose of the old webhook** (delete recommended) and record the decision.
7. **Document** the channel + config precedence + verification command in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` ("Deployment / Release" section) and keep the config comment accurate.
8. **Confirm at the next release** that the announcement appears in the new channel (observation recorded on this item), then hand over for review.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.worklog/config.private.yaml` — the single live routing config; replace `discord.webhook_url`, add a channel-naming comment, keep mode `0600`. (Gitignored — never committed.)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Deployment / Release" section gains a short "Release notifications (Discord)" subsection: channel, config precedence, verification command, secret handling.
- `RELEASE.md` — optional one-line cross-reference to the new notification section during the release checklist.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` and `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — **read-only reference** for precedence (`resolveDiscordWebhookUrl`), payload composition and the non-blocking contract; no change expected.
- `.gitignore` — read-only confirmation that `.worklog/` (and therefore the private config) is ignored.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: announcing into the wrong channel** (internal vs community-facing server). Mitigation: verify `channel_id` from the webhook probe and post a test message before the next release; the server choice is the Producer's explicit decision (Appendix).
- **Risk: leaking the webhook token** into a commit, comment or log. Mitigation: never paste the token, record `[REDACTED]`, confirm `.worklog/` stays gitignored, keep the file at `0600`.
- **Risk: duplicate announcements** if the old webhook stays active and is also consumed elsewhere. Mitigation: explicit disposition step; searched the TCE repo — no other reference to the old webhook exists.
- **Risk: routing silently breaks and is only noticed at the next release.** Mitigation: repeatable verification command documented, plus a post-release confirmation AC.

data.description:
# Core UI: WebGL-safe clipping for HelpPanel, Overlay and SettingsPanel scroll content

**Issue type:** `bug` · **Priority:** `medium` · **Stage target:** `intake_complete`
**Cross-repo:** blocks `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` (tce-main-street — Core UI: `GeometryMask` `setMask` is a no-op under WebGL); parent of that defect is `MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM`.

## Goal

As a player running the game on the WebGL renderer, I want the help panel,
parameterised overlay and settings panel scroll content clipped to its visible
scroll area, so overflowing text no longer draws over the panel chrome and the
rest of the scene.

## Problem statement

Phaser 4 (`4.0.0-rc.7`) makes `GameObject.setMask()` with a `GeometryMask` a
no-op under WebGL — it logs and returns immediately:

```js
// node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js
setMask: function (mask) {
    if (this.scene.renderer.type === CONST.WEBGL) {
        console.warn('Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.');
        return this;
    }
```

Core UI uses that API for all three of its scrollable surfaces, so under a
WebGL boot (`createCardGame` defaults to `Phaser.AUTO`,
`core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts:123`) the content is not clipped at all. Under
Canvas the masks work correctly and the current suite exercises that path, so
the regression is invisible to tests today.

## Users

- **Player on a WebGL boot** — "when I open the help panel, the text spills
  over the panel border and covers the game behind it."
- **Game developer / engine maintainer** — "I need core UI to clip its scroll
  areas the same way on both renderers, so a game can choose WebGL without
  visual regressions."

## Call sites in scope

| File | Line (pin `f0b5b9e`) | Call |
|---|---|---|
| `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` | 523-524 | `this.contentMask = new GeometryMask(...)`; `this.contentContainer.setMask(this.contentMask)` |
| `src/ui/Overlay.ts` | 484 | `scrollContainer.setMask(maskGraphics.createGeometryMask())` (plus `clearMask()` in the else branch) |
| `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` | 909-910 | `this._scrollContent.setMask(new GeometryMask(scene, maskGraphics))` |

## Existing state (verified against the pin)

- `core` submodule pin: `f0b5b9e9` (`v0.1.22-1`), `core/package.json` → `phaser: 4.0.0-rc.7`.
- No core UI test asserts clipping; the three masks are created inside panel
  setup helpers (`setupScrollMask` in `HelpPanel`, `refresh()` in `Overlay`,
  the `_maxContentY > canvasHeight` branch in `SettingsPanel`).
- Core already has a precedent for booting a scene under a chosen renderer in
  browser tests: `tests/gym/GymGraphicsLightingSpikeScene.browser.test.ts`
  `bootScene(renderType)` boots both `Phaser.CANVAS` and `Phaser.WEBGL`. It is
  the only core test that mentions `Phaser.WEBGL`.
- Browser test infrastructure: `@vitest/browser` + `@vitest/browser-playwright`
  (headless Chromium), `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Adopt the renderer-branched clipping pattern established by the in-repo
   Main Street work (`MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM`, mechanism decided by
   `MS-0MVTE3JFB002XOW8`) — do not invent a second mechanism.
2. Keep the Canvas path **byte-identical** in behaviour: the existing
   `GeometryMask` creation stays exactly as-is on Canvas.
3. On WebGL, clip the three containers with the chosen mechanism (Mask filter,
   dedicated camera viewport, or equivalent) and update it on scroll/resize
   the same way the mask graphics is updated today.
4. Tear down the WebGL clip alongside the existing mask teardown so repeated
   panel open/close does not leak filters, cameras or graphics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HelpPanel`'s `contentContainer`, `Overlay`'s `scrollContainer` and
  `SettingsPanel`'s `_scrollContent` are clipped to their scroll area under a
  real WebGL boot — verified by a browser test that boots each panel with
  `type: Phaser.WEBGL` and asserts content outside the scroll rect is not
  rendered (pixel/scroll-position assertion, not a mock).
- No `setMask … not supported in WebGL` console warning is emitted when each of
  the three panels is opened under a WebGL boot (console assertion in the
  browser test).
- The same three panels remain correctly clipped under a Canvas boot, and the
  existing Canvas-path tests are unmodified and green (Canvas `GeometryMask`
  call sites still exercised).
- WebGL clip teardown is covered: closing/reopening a panel (and destroying the
  scene) leaves no orphaned filter/camera/graphics, asserted in the same
  browser test.
- `npm run build` (tsc `--noEmit` + vite build) and the core test suite pass.

## Constraints

- `core` is a submodule of `tce-main-street` — this change lands in the engine
  repo (`TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`, `dev` branch), not in the game
  repo.
- Renderer branch, not a wholesale replacement: Canvas output must stay
  byte-stable (the majority of games and tests boot Canvas).
- No public API change to `HelpPanel` / `Overlay` / `SettingsPanel` constructors
  or options — the renderer choice must stay internal.
- Do not change panel layout, scroll speeds, track-bar geometry or panel
  dimensions; clipping only.
- Out of scope: the launcher/core boot renderer switch (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`),
  Main Street's own viewport masks, and the gym scenes.

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by `MS-0MVTE3JFB002XOW8` (Main Street spike, "choose the WebGL
  container-clip mechanism"): the mechanism and its limits must be decided
  before this work starts, since this item reuses it.
- Reference implementation: `MS-0MVTE3LIA003K3EA` (street map viewport clip
  under WebGL) — consult its diff for the concrete pattern once landed.

## Deliverables

- Core commit(s) on the engine `dev` branch with the three renderer-branched
  clips + browser tests.
- The engine commit SHA recorded on `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW`.

## Test Plan

- New browser test(s) under `core/tests/ui/` booting the three panels with
  `type: Phaser.WEBGL` and `type: Phaser.CANVAS`: assertion of clipping, absence
  of the `setMask` warning, and teardown.
- `npx vitest run <the new test files>` plus the existing `tests/ui` suite.
- `npm run build`.
- Manual check: `npm run dev` in the engine repo, open the help panel and
  settings panel, confirm no clipping regression and no console warning.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — `setupScrollMask` (~512-525), mask graphics
  update on scroll, teardown.
- `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts` — `refresh()` mask apply/clear branch (~479-487).
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — `_scrollContent` mask setup (~896-911) and
  wheel/scroll handler.
- `core/tests/ui/HelpSettingsButtons.test.ts`, `Overlay.test.ts`,
  `SettingsPanel.test.ts` — existing Canvas-path coverage to keep green.
- `core/tests/gym/GymGraphicsLightingSpikeScene.browser.test.ts` — the
  renderer-parameterised boot harness to model new WebGL browser tests on.
- `core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts` — renderer default (`AUTO`) context for the
  test boot.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — mask/filter availability on the target containers.** The Main Street
  spike exists precisely because `FilterList` may not be mixed into
  `Container`. If the final mechanism is a dedicated camera viewport, three
  extra cameras may be needed; cost/limits must be recorded. Mitigation: wait
  for the spike's decision, reuse it verbatim.
- **Risk — WebGL in headless CI.** A WebGL boot needs a working headless
  Chromium WebGL context; the suite must degrade loudly (skip with a recorded
  reason) rather than silently pass. Mitigation: follow the existing
  `GymGraphicsLightingSpikeScene` boot pattern and assert
  `renderer.type === Phaser.WEBGL` in the test setup.
- **Risk — `SettingsPanel` mask is in scene space and positioned for the
  panel's slide-in.** A camera-viewport approach must track the slide
  animation; the filter approach must be re-positioned per frame with the
  panel. Mitigation: assert clipping at both the open and slid-in positions.
- **Assumption — the WebGL clip is visually identical to the Canvas
  `GeometryMask` clip.** Clipping rect = the same rect the mask graphics draws
  today.
- **Assumption — the mechanism chosen for `Container`s in Main Street is
  applicable here**: `contentContainer`, `scrollContainer` and
  `_scrollContent` are all containers.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the audit may reveal further `GeometryMask` uses in core
  (gym scenes, example games). Those are out of scope — record them as linked
  work items rather than widening this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` — the Main Street coordination item this satisfies.
- `MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM` — parent defect (Phaser 4 + WebGL `GeometryMask`
  no-op), source of the fix pattern.
- `MS-0MVTE3JFB002XOW8` — mechanism spike (blocked-by).
- `MS-0MVTE3LIA003K3EA`, `MS-0MVTE3MJM007K75W`, `MS-0MVTE3NLP0031XM2` — the
  sibling in-repo clips (street, Activity Log, gym card index).
- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` — deferred Canvas→WebGL renderer migration for Main
  Street (scope split: that item owns the boot switch and test-project
  plumbing).
- `CG-0MLTAOG6U1SDSFHI` — "Scrollable Content with Track Bar" (origin of the
  `HelpPanel`/`Overlay` scroll-mask design).
- `CG-0MPD5XW6G000F7W9` — "Gym Graphics: Geometry Masks / Clipping" (the
  Canvas-side clipping reference).
- Duplicate check performed in both worklogs (`GeometryMask`, `setMask`,
  `scroll clipping mask`, `mask webgl`) — no existing or completed core item
  covers WebGL-safe clipping of these three panels.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Questions are recorded here with the agent's recommendation; no blocking
question required a producer answer before drafting (see "Assumptions" above).

- Q: Which of the three requested blurs should ship first? — Not applicable;
  all three sites share one mechanism and ship together.
- Q: Should this work wait for the Main Street spike? — Answer (agent,
  code/wl evidence): yes. `MS-0MVTE3JFB002XOW8` is still `open`/`intake_complete`
  and the parent records that the mechanism is unproven for `Container`s.
  **Recommended:** block this item on that spike. Source: `wl list --parent
  MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM`, `wl show MS-0MVTE3JFB002XOW8`.
- Q: Which renderer must the fix preserve? — Answer (code, verified): Canvas.
  `createCardGame` defaults to `AUTO` (`core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts:123`), so
  the shipped Main Street launcher (`index.html` → `main.ts`) is Canvas today;
  most games and tests boot Canvas, so its output must stay unchanged.
- Q: Does core already have a WebGL browser-test harness? — Answer (code,
  verified): yes, a limited one —
  `tests/gym/GymGraphicsLightingSpikeScene.browser.test.ts` boots both
  `Phaser.CANVAS` and `Phaser.WEBGL` with `@vitest/browser`/playwright. It is
  the only `Phaser.WEBGL` reference in the core repo.
- Q: Is the pinned version the one with the defect? — Answer (code, verified):
  yes, `core/package.json` pins `phaser: 4.0.0-rc.7`, the version whose
  `Mask.setMask` short-circuits under WebGL; pin `f0b5b9e9` (`v0.1.22-1`)
  matches the `./core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json`.
